purpose: Measure one reference pure-F vertical slice without promoting a broad runtime or engine.
owned_mechanism: Validate one explicit snapshot and accepted observation event.
Derive one signed base FactDelta and zero or one authority-free EffectProposal.
Return a fresh next snapshot or a closed typed rejection without mutating inputs.
Derive identities and digests only from versioned canonical explicit input.
excluded_policy_and_authority: Capability, approval, EffectIntent, dispatch, receipt, retry, and reconciliation
Persistence, ports, adapters, registries, plugins, and model or tool execution
transition_rules: The event aggregate_id and expected_revision must match the snapshot.
The full version envelope must match and the supported workflow, state, event, and canonicalization versions must be exact.
Logical time may stay equal or advance; it may not regress.
A closed snapshot rejects every observation event.
mark_complete closes the returned snapshot after recording the observation.
output_invariants: Every FactDelta has diff +1, event logical_time, event_id causation, and the event rule-set and dataflow versions.
Every EffectProposal has event cause and correlation, event versions, an action digest bound to explicit action data, and a destination digest bound to explicit destination data.
Every derivation, proposal, and proposal-dedup identity binds the complete emitted value except its own identity field or fields.
EffectProposal preconditions are unique and emitted in canonical-byte order.
F output contains no EffectIntent, capability, authority, assessed risk, approval, adapter binding, final effect idempotency key, or execution receipt.
Success and rejection return fresh JSON values and leave both caller inputs byte-for-byte unchanged.

identity_preimages.value_rule: The value is the complete canonical emitted FactDelta or EffectProposal content with only its self-referential identity field or fields omitted.

digest_note: Each nested FactDelta and EffectProposal is canonicalized at its own root kind before its digest enters the projection; the transition never assumes wildcard set semantics.
completion_gate: The frozen success and rejection corpus validates against closed schemas.
Two spawned clean processes with distinct hash seed, timezone, cwd, and ambient environment produce byte-identical canonical results.
Malformed and incompatible inputs return the expected typed rejection and never mutate input.

A trusted test loader preloads and compiles source, then a fresh-process audit hook plus explicit Python surface traps lock ambient access before any implementation module body executes; every guarded category has a positive self-test, guarded kernel attempts remain zero, and deliberate ambient and mutation mutants are detected.
Independent semantic construction and frozen canonical golden bytes agree with both transition and rejection output.
Every emitted FactDelta and EffectProposal validates against protocol.v1 and no H-owned object or field is emitted.
completion_boundary: Passing M1 measures only the declared Python reference kernel, frozen corpus, instrumented ambient surfaces, and tested environments. It is not a proof of universal purity, L/R/H mechanics, integrated runtime behavior, production readiness, comparative efficacy, or Lakatos progress.
